epic.intent:
Implement a fully local procedural campaign system for Mount & Blade II: Bannerlord with War Sails. From Bannerlord's New Campaign screen, the player chooses a seed/settings, generates a new FWGC++ world, and enters that world's terrain, settlements, factions, characters, economy and naval routes. Saving and loading must bind the correct immutable world to each campaign. The user explicitly requires in-game generation, full generated campaign content and naval travel; an external generator/editor/build/relaunch workflow does not satisfy this epic. This is an implementation plan, not evidence that Bannerlord supports all necessary runtime operations. Prove runtime terrain, water, navmesh, object registration and campaign-load hooks on the installed version before building the production pipeline. Record an unsupported operation as a blocked gate with evidence; do not silently substitute a static map. All future source/file/command names not found in the current repository are proposed implementation contracts.

Confirmed presentation: full generated globe as a flat map with connected east/west edges. Reuse existing Bannerlord and War Sails character, troop, building and mission assets while generating world names, identities and relationships. Custom race/art production and a rotatable 3D globe are not required.

successCriteria.text: A pinned FWGC++ build and version-matched Bannerlord/Modding Kit/War Sails setup are reproducibly identified and verified; the existing stale generator binary is not accepted as installation evidence.

Bannerlord's New Campaign flow generates a fresh chosen-seed world locally with progress/cancel/error handling, without a player running an external editor, publishing a module or restarting the game.

The entire generated globe is playable as a flat map with connected east/west edges. Terrain, player/AI land and naval routes, distances, encounters, camera/picking and saves use one consistent periodic topology; different seeds change geography and traversability.

Generated towns, villages, castles, factions, clans and characters initialize a coherent Sandbox campaign with trading, recruitment, ownership, wars and missions, with no unintended Calradia campaign objects surviving.
War Sails ports, fleets, embarkation, land/sea routes, navigation types and required distance caches operate on the generated world; naval travel and naval encounters are tested.

Two campaigns with different world identities can be saved, alternately loaded after a cold restart, and resumed with correct terrain, objects and navigation; missing or mismatched worlds fail safely before simulation.

A clean packaged installation completes the specified new-world, land/naval gameplay, simulation, persistence, cancellation and performance matrix with evidence; budgets are measured and accepted before release.

bundle.rationale:
# Execution contract and current status

This is a detailed implementation plan. No Bannerlord runtime prototype, FWGC++ rebuild, map replacement or game test was performed during planning. Source/API research identifies credible candidates, not proof that the requested runtime system is possible. The installed game and kit were incomplete when inspected. All production tickets depend on a passing runtime feasibility review. If that fails, report the exact missing engine capability; do not call an external editor workflow an implementation of this request.

## Confirmed user requirements

- FWGC++ is the existing local C++ project at C:/Users/davgo/Documents/GitHub/FWGC++.
- A different generated world must be possible for each new campaign.
- Generation must happen inside Bannerlord's New Campaign flow. The player must not launch another tool, run a per-seed editor bake, publish a module, or restart the game.
- Replace both geography and campaign content with FWGC++-derived content.
- War Sails naval gameplay is mandatory.
- The implementation plan lives in Dark Mechanicus and must be detailed enough to guide execution without guessing.

The user confirmed the ENTIRE generated globe represented as a FLAT map with CONNECTED EAST/WEST EDGES, and approved reuse of Bannerlord/War Sails character, troop, building and mission assets for generated content. No regional crop, disconnected seam, actual rotatable 3D globe or custom fantasy asset production is required. F03 records these decisions; R10 proves periodic topology in the shipping client. Proposed initial game mode is a custom Sandbox campaign; StoryMode narrative integration is an explicit additional decision, because the story has world-specific dependencies. Multiplayer, the FWGC++ dialogue/director/LLM stack, and entirely generated combat mechanics are not implied by this request.

## Inspected facts and their consequences

The coordinating repository initially contains .gitattributes, .mcp.json and .darkmechanicus metadata, with no mod source or build system. Dark Mechanicus 0.18.0 reports no existing epics/profiles and an empty project Definition of Done. This epic was created through the supported planner MCP role with plan.save; no run was started.

FWGC++ source was clean at ec5d1c10f5ae4c32fdcef092d23ad7d51e2a30de. The existing executable at generator/build/apps/Release/fwg.exe runs help but is older than HEAD and omits the current source weather command. Rebuild and hash it; presence is not installation proof. Generator is C++20, CMake >=3.20, with no third-party generator dependency and no install() target. The local Visual Studio BuildTools distribution includes CMake outside PATH. A producer-only install does not require inference, training, Vulkan models or NPC dialogue components.

Current source exposes JSON generation, not Bannerlord/PNG/RAW/scene/navmesh export. Its world is spherical. The surface-city maximum is 24; it is validated in generator/src/config.cpp and constrained in settlements_stage.cpp. Bigger raster size does not remove the cap. The public read_patch surface is bounded local terrain, not a whole-world exporter; an internal export_height_tile must not be used as if public. Source runtime guardrails require consumer-specific adaptation outside FWGC++; this repository owns the Bannerlord bridge. Any truly needed upstream extension must be generic, follow FWGC++ AGENTS, pass its gates, and land before its consumer; no such extension is presumed here.

Producer command contract (existing): fwg.exe generate --request <request.json> --split <fresh-directory> --quiet. Request uses seed, recipe_version 3 and overrides. Source root uses schema fwg.world, schema_version 2, split.version 1. Verify capabilities and block versions against the pinned binary. Refusals can return a failure document with exit 2; do not parse it as a world. Avoid --timings in deterministic payloads. Full JSON can be hundreds of MB; split world.json still holds large layers. The C++ bridge must stream selected content and respect measured memory bounds.

The source grid is n by n, north-to-south, duplicate seam column. longitude = -180 + 360*x/(n-1); latitude = 90 - 180*z/(n-1). Source graph node indices collapse poles/seam, so they require a separate decoder. Height is radial elevation relative to the source sphere; sea-relative height subtracts effective_config.sea_level. effective_config and layers are physical metres; config is design space. The source layout seed is a decimal string, and must remain exact. Keep stable UIDs, not ordinal IDs or names.

Official documentation establishes editor terrain import and scene overrides. It does NOT prove runtime terrain construction. Public runtime API candidates include procedural meshes, navigation prefab operations, map-scene creation, object registration and cache generation; each is version-sensitive and must be executed in the shipping client. No general public heightfield setter was established in research. Native map picking, face records and DLC consumers can bypass a custom IMapScene, so implementing an interface alone is insufficient.

Current XML records merge by unique ID. Supplying a smaller settlements file does not remove the old campaign. A runtime custom-mode registration strategy must own the complete world object graph, distinguish reusable definitions from world instances, and run before references/default lists/behaviors require it. Supported removal transforms are not a substitute for proving per-campaign registration timing.

War Sails adds typed sea navigation, separate port/dropoff positions and naval-aware distance models. Official setup identifies town_port/main_map_city_port, village drop_point/main_map_village_dropoff, blockade anchors and custom naval water resources. Lakes are impassable; directed path costs can differ. Exact enum numbers, scripts, flow formats and native lifecycle are installed-build contracts. The docs describe editor cache rebuilds; the in-game equivalent still needs proof. Use primary sources listed below and the local fixture inventory.

## Proposed architecture (conditional on Sprint 2)

1. MNBL.ProceduralWorld C# host: module integration, New Campaign UI, job coordination, game-manager/object bootstrap, engine-thread work, runtime scene/navigation implementation, DLC integration and save/load. Compile against the actual installed target framework/assemblies; do not hardcode a historical framework. Reference game/DLC binaries locally without redistributing them.
2. worldbridge.exe C++20 worker in src/WorldBridge: supervised fwg producer, streaming schema reader, projection, static terrain/content/nav-intent compilation, deterministic validation and immutable bundle writer. This process isolates large memory workloads and crashes. It never calls engine APIs or mutates game objects.
3. Pinned fwg.exe: source generation only, in a child process started automatically by the in-game host/bridge. A process boundary is compatible with the requested UX; a player-operated external workflow is not.
4. Reusable shipped resources: bootstrap scene, materials, scene/prefab/navigation building blocks, UI and approved character/mission assets. The kit may author/publish these during development. No per-campaign kit launch, asset publishing or manual copying is permitted in the player workflow.
5. Per-user world store: immutable source/compiler data, separately keyed backend/navigation artifacts, save bindings, manifests and diagnostic run records. Suggested writable root is %LOCALAPPDATA%/MNBL.ProceduralWorld. Game install folders and official modules remain owned by Steam. Final root and any save-sidecar path are tested on the installed version.

Runtime backend candidates are bounded experiments, not parallel production architectures. Prefer supported native terrain if a callable path is proven. Otherwise test procedural mesh geometry plus verified query/collision handling and native navigation prefab assembly. A custom IMapScene/routing backend may be considered only if every direct native consumer and naval system is proved compatible. No invented binary writer, binary patching or undocumented setter is presumed. R07 selects one backend. Later tickets implement that recorded contract or stop; they do not guess around an unsupported operation.

## Interface and artifact contracts

All following names are proposed files to implement, not present tooling.

- tools.lock.json / producer.lock.json: exact source commit, binary SHA-256, compiler/UCRT/CMake, schema/capability snapshots and dependencies. Choose one canonical ownership location during F04/FWG-01; if a consumer copy exists it must be derived and checked, never an independently editable duplicate.
- GenerationRequest v1: jobId, campaignInstanceId, seed text with producer-verified numeric width, recipeVersion, explicit overrides, requested profile, producerLockHash, policyHashes and attempt policy. Reject unknown required fields. Record exact request bytes. Preserve deliberate same-seed replay; Random World requests a fresh seed.
- ProgressEvent v1: jobId, monotonically increasing sequence, phase, completed/total when measurable, messageCode and optional typed error. stdout protocol framing and bounded stderr diagnostics are distinct. The host discards late events after cancellation or another job's activation.
- SourceWorld v1: validated selected layer streams and stable UID records with source-block versions, provenance, explicit optional fields and unsupported-field dispositions. Follow split file indices; never reconstruct sanitized filenames.
- Projection v1: full declared coverage, source sphere radius, seam/pole policy, transform/version, target bounds, axis/row orientation, horizontal scale, vertical origin/scale, sea datum and inverse mapping. A single implementation supplies every terrain/entity/route/port/spawn transform. Control-point and seam fixtures accompany the contract.
- CampaignDefinition v1: stable IDs/source UIDs, realms/cultures/clans/heroes, settlement kinds/parents/owners/locations/economy, troop/template references, spawn and naval intents. Synthesized data has an explicit policy version and provenance. Undefined mappings fail. Source population does not directly become prosperity, and source bridge candidates do not automatically become traversable bridges.
- WorldDataBundle v1: versioned relative-path inventory, lengths/hashes, source/request/projection/policy/compiler identity, static validation reports and DATA_READY marker. WorldContentId hashes deterministic content; campaign instance identity and volatile timings stay outside that content hash to allow replay/deduplication.
- RuntimeDerivedBundle v1: selected backend version, game/DLC/asset fingerprints, native scene/navigation CRCs where needed, resolved gate/port positions, generated resources, caches and actual route-validation report. Native pointers/face handles are never portable IDs. Changes invalidate the appropriate derived artifact.
- ActivationReceipt v1: this campaign instance accepted this content and compatible runtime bundle after all object, terrain, navigation, scene and naval checks passed. Filesystem publication alone does not mean activation.
- SaveBinding v1: stable save identity, campaign instance, content/runtime bundle identities, compatibility contract and journal state. It must be discoverable before scene/object reconstruction. Later SyncData alone cannot be assumed to solve early bootstrap. Save A and save B can share content intentionally but never mutable state.

## Coordinate, topology and content rules

World coverage is fixed: the complete source globe, flat periodic east/west map. One canonical logical world may have repeated display strips, but native routes, AI distances, encounters, picking, camera and saves must share that topology. R10 proves seam travel and pole representation; W07 implements it. No regional crop, disconnected edge or player-only teleport counts as completion.

Continuous layers use suitable continuous sampling; categorical biomes and navigation classes never interpolate enum numbers. Source and output resolution are separate: upsampling cannot invent lost topography. If a backend requires 16-bit heights, use a single recorded global range, explicit orientation/byte order and a reconstruction bound of half one quantization step plus numeric tolerance. Adjacent tiles share sampled boundaries. Visual ocean, gameplay water and navigation domain all reference the same sea datum.

The semantic mapping begins with settlements.sites UIDs (town candidates), humans.hamlets UIDs (rural/harbour variants), humans.fortresses UIDs (castle candidates), and heroes.realms capital/city/sovereign relationships. Validate nullable sovereigns, missing names and variant rural records. Road endpoints may be settlement array indices; normalize them to stable UIDs immediately. Every gameplay record retains provenance to source or declared synthesis. Complete generated content means reference-closed factions/heroes/settlements/parties/naval records; it does not mean source JSON already contains Bannerlord-ready definitions.

Navigation is typed connectivity, not one flood fill. Record land components, sea basins, crossings, allowed shoreline transitions and party capabilities. A required island can remain playable through verified maritime connections. A land-only caravan route cannot be validated with a ship-only edge. The engine's actual routes decide playability after placement; the compiler graph is an intent and preflight check. All gate/port/dropoff changes invalidate distance caches. Path distances may be directed.

## Transaction and failure semantics

Conceptual pipeline: request validation -> source generation -> conversion -> static validation -> scene/navigation realization and staged object registration in the proven order -> runtime validation -> preview/character selection as allowed by lifecycle -> commit -> simulation. One job owns temporary paths and process/resources. Cancellation cannot kill unrelated processes or delete another world's files. Main-thread native work is chunked where supported; background workers never write engine handles directly.

Quality retries are bounded and deterministic with explicit attempt numbers and derived seeds, only when the accepted policy allows them. A schema error, compiler crash or missing engine capability is not a bad seed and must fail immediately. The UI reports the final chosen seed and rejection reasons. Never silently substitute Calradia or use a prebuilt map. Do not regenerate old saves from seed; source determinism is tied to the complete generator/toolchain/config/version, and engine state includes more than source generation.

World activation requires DATA_READY plus actual runtime validation and an activation receipt. Immutable definitions remain separate from mutable campaign simulation. Save/load discovers identity before engine object deserialization; create/register and reconstruct resources before references are consumed. Derived caches can be rebuilt only by a tested compatible path from frozen data. Original missing/corrupt definitions fail safely. An update does not silently migrate IDs or rewrite saves.

## Required evidence and test strategy

Use a minimal genuine runtime vertical slice first. It must start from the real New Campaign flow, generate two source seeds, change geometry and traversability, initialize generated world objects, move land and naval parties, and save/load A/B in the same process and after restart. Test failure cases while the menu/earlier saves remain intact. An API listing, successful compiler build, pretty map screenshot or separate graph validator cannot substitute for this evidence.

Targeted tests accompany each actual component. The final gate collects current accepted evidence instead of rerunning every expensive suite at every ticket. Synthetic tests independently check schema failures, seed precision, seam/pole transforms, categorical sampling, stable ID joins, dangling references, travel domains and transactional publication. Runtime acceptance covers player and AI movement, economy/recruitment, wars/sieges/succession, land/naval mission entry-return, all present scene types, weather/season behavior and save compatibility. Use at least 20 compiler fixtures and five runtime worlds, plus explicit bad cases; these are proposed test coverage counts, not performance claims. The acceptance checkpoint can increase coverage if observed failures justify it.

Proposed soak coverage is 100 campaign days on at least three accepted worlds and ten repeated create/cancel/load cycles; include manual seasonal samples even if that day count does not span all seasons. Track route failures, stuck parties, missing IDs, out-of-bounds coordinates, resource growth and errors. Treat the duration as a test specification, not as completed evidence. Exact runtime budgetsâ€”generation time, peak memory/disk, per-frame/simulation cost, load/save timeâ€”are set from R06/Q03 measurements on this machine and accepted before release. No arbitrary latency promise has been made.

## Execution graph, ownership and checkpoints

Sprint 1 pins tools/contracts and captures the baseline. F02 source rebuild and F03 decisions can proceed independently of game download completion; runtime shell/baseline wait for installed assets.
Sprint 2 proves the full runtime architecture and is the critical gate. R02 surface and R04 data boot can proceed independently after R01; R03 joins them for real party/naval travel, then R08 environment rebinding and R09 mission transitions, R05 persistence, R06 measurements and R07 review.
Sprint 3 implements deterministic source conversion. Process/identity work precedes parsing and projection; terrain/semantic branches join in static travel intent and bundle output. Runtime validation is deliberately deferred to the host to avoid dependency cycles.
Sprint 4 instantiates and validates the full campaign object graph. Sprint 5 realizes surface/nav/water/entities/caches/missions through the selected backend. Sprint 6 delivers the production in-game UX and transactional commit. Sprint 7 proves persistence and gameplay breadth. Sprint 8 sweeps seeds/faults and measures proposed production profiles. Its human checkpoint approves the final budgets/settings. Sprint 9 packages and documents the approved release; packaging never waits on an approval trapped behind its own sprint acceptance.

Every sprint has one automatically created Dark Mechanicus acceptance node with a covers criterion for every required work ticket; no artificial edge is added into acceptance. Human checkpoints remain human. Acceptance owns combined verification and the sprint integration increment; there is no redundant merge-everything ticket. Code/data work may use two workers with disjoint paths, but the live game/editor is a single-owner resource. Workers must release/acknowledge control; a handoff is not completion. Do not hold a shared editor while waiting on source work. No worker gets permission to modify unrelated source or official installs.

The initial project Definition of Done is empty; this plan does not invent a Fireguard command from the Dark Mechanicus application's own repo. F04 establishes the actual mod build/test commands. Acceptance runs applicable current checks plus the sprint's runtime criteria. Epic branch selection/creation occurs during execution under repository rules (codex/ default if a new branch is needed); planning does not change Git branches or start a run.

## Expanded official-documentation audit: implementation consequences

Research was deepened across independent navigation/naval, object/save lifecycle and mission/asset reviews. Documentation versions are reference material; installation probes remain authoritative. No complete runtime procedural-world or periodic-map recipe was found. The plan therefore distinguishes documented members from a passing shipping-client capability.

The wrapping design must adapt route execution, strategic distances/caches and spatial proximity separately. IMapScene route methods are candidates; PartyNavigationModel is a capability/permission policy. Native party path points do not establish seam-aware movement. R10 proves this, W07 owns canonical coordinates/distances, W08 actual movement/spatial queries, and W09 camera/picking/display copies. MapCameraView exposes useful camera extension methods, which must be exercised under the installed build.

Object generation must happen at the right registration phase and also support the loaded-game path. R04 traces initialization/default-list timing, C01 owns registry ordering, and R05/U06/P01-P03 prove save identity before deserialization. Existing module XML merging describes loading semantics, not a complete dynamic-world reset protocol.

Mission selection has documented SceneModel map-patch and conversation methods; use them if the R09 probe passes. Terrain/patch position, naval flag, encounter direction, atmosphere and scene levels must agree. Wrapped shortest attacker-defender displacement is required near the seam. W06/P06 include seaborne village raids in addition to naval field battles; each reused scene must have compatible levels, hierarchy, tags, spawns and return paths.

Reusable assets must remain references to installed owned modules. Static published reusable templates may be authored with the kit, while every generated world must still be constructed inside the game. Test clean packaged Client assets without editor/development source paths. Exact object/scene schemas and APIs are pinned in the installed-version evidence rather than copied from old tutorials.

## Documentation review additions and provenance

The deep dive added fixed module save IDs versus per-world object IDs; save metadata/lifecycle candidates; complete naval culture references; the fact that raw PartyBase construction is not campaign registration; whole ship/prefab contracts; periodic nearby-party/encounter queries independent of path distance; current map-patch/mission initialization interfaces; seaborne raid, siege-state and hideout transition scenarios; scene-level/script lifecycle constraints; and clean Client-package tests.
